sources.title: Climate Change Vulnerability Analyses and Mapping for National Adaptation Plan Formulation Process in Bhutan
sources.organization: Royal Government of Bhutan and United Nations Development Programme Bhutan
sources.temporal_coverage: Dzongkhag indicators mainly from 2005-2017 and hazard records from 2010-2018; future risk modeled at five-year intervals to 2050.
sources.methodology: Dzongkhag indices combine government hazard/socioeconomic indicators and stakeholder input.
sources.limitations: Older sparse local data limit temporal/causal precision; projections exclude wildcard events.

sources.title: Assessment of Climate-Induced Loss and Damage in Bhutan
sources.organization: Department of Environment and Climate Change, Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources, Royal Government of Bhutan, and United Nations Development Programme Bhutan
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 assessment drawing on historical records, 2024 field visits, and observed events through October 2025.
sources.methodology: Government-UNDP assessment used interviews, workshops, site visits and triangulation.
sources.limitations: Fragmented, undercounted loss records; human-mobility links are sometimes anecdotal.

sources.title: Kingdom of Bhutan, First National Adaptation Plan 2023
sources.organization: Department of Environment and Climate Change, Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources, Royal Government of Bhutan
sources.temporal_coverage: National adaptation priorities and implementation needs for the medium and long term; document published in 2023.
sources.methodology: The NAP synthesizes four sectoral risk assessments and national and regional stakeholder consultations.
sources.limitations: Adaptation priorities are policy commitments, not verified nationwide service outcomes.

sources.title: Mid Term Review of Advancing Climate Resilience of the Water Sector in Bhutan (ACREWAS)
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme and Royal Government of Bhutan, Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport
sources.temporal_coverage: Midterm review submitted in February 2026 for a project running from September 2023 to September 2028.
sources.methodology: Non-experimental review used documents, interviews, focus groups and observations.
sources.limitations: Midterm project evidence; some water-access and watershed outcomes were not yet delivered.

claims.paraphrase: The present-risk index ranks Samtse, Monggar, Sarpang, Punakha and Dagana highest after combining hazards, exposure, population density and vulnerability.
claims.limitations: Composite ranking using older administrative indicators, not a measured loss estimate.

claims.paraphrase: Zhemgang, Dagana and Gasa had the lowest adaptive-capacity scores; the assessment says they may recover more slowly and need external support after extremes.
claims.limitations: Index proxies capacity using available socioeconomic indicators; recovery outcomes were not measured.

claims.locator: Printed p. 52, section 5.1.3, Gewog Vulnerability Recommendations
claims.paraphrase: Lunana gewog in Gasa ranked most socioeconomically vulnerable; the report cites very low electricity access and only about 19% concrete housing.
claims.limitations: Relative composite vulnerability ranking, not a household-level climate-impact estimate.

claims.locator: Printed p. 52, section 5.1.2, Future Climate Risk Recommendations
claims.paraphrase: Thimphu is projected as the highest future-risk area, associated with in-migration, urbanisation and population growth.
claims.scenario: Model to 2050 uses RCP4.5/RCP8.5; Thimphu summary does not specify one.
claims.limitations: No wildcard events modeled; new development could change risk.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Report links Thimphu's higher projected climate risk to in-migration, urbanisation and population growth.

claims.locator: Printed p. 45, section 4.2, Food and Water Insecurity
claims.paraphrase: Report says climate-related farmland and water loss often drives distress rural-to-urban migration.
claims.limitations: Report calls this often anecdotal; no mobility counts or conflict evidence are given.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate-related loss of farmland and water is linked to distress rural-to-urban migration.

claims.locator: Printed p. 61, section on terrestrial and freshwater ecosystem impacts
claims.paraphrase: Assessment links climate-driven wetland and habitat shifts with increased human-wildlife conflict.
claims.limitations: This is human-wildlife conflict, not evidence of interpersonal or political violence; incidents are not quantified.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate-related habitat and species shifts are linked to heightened human-wildlife conflict risk.

claims.locator: Printed p. 74, Case Study 1: Dechencholing flood
claims.paraphrase: The 2024 Dechencholing flood displaced 84 families, closed two schools and killed one person; the report says it affected wellbeing and social cohesion.
claims.limitations: Single urban case study; displacement duration and subsequent group-level outcomes are not quantified.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Flood displacement and school disruption affected community wellbeing and social cohesion.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 75-76, Case Study 2: Punakha flash floods
claims.paraphrase: 2025 Punakha floods cut Gasa road access for over two weeks; bridge loss affected 42 households, while budget gaps delayed response and residents supplied most repair labour.
claims.limitations: Visited-village case; livelihood, health and education losses remain largely unaccounted for.

claims.locator: PDF p. 19, Executive Summary, Water-sector adaptation priorities
claims.paraphrase: The NAP prioritizes protecting and managing water sources, water-user groups, local stakeholder capacity, research and integrated water management across sectors.
claims.limitations: These are national adaptation priorities, not measured delivery or service outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 38-39, Table 6, GEF 7 Climate Change Adaptation Results Framework
claims.paraphrase: At midterm, ACREWAS reported 11,544 beneficiaries (45.7% female), 3,220 trained people and 4,426 hectares under climate-resilient management.
claims.limitations: Interim project indicators, not independent measurements of household-level resilience or long-term impact.

claims.locator: PDF p. 29, Finding 8, Indicator 8 on assured water access
claims.paraphrase: Only 5.6% of the midterm target for people with assured irrigation and domestic-water access was achieved while systems remained under construction.
claims.limitations: The MTR says beneficiary counts cannot be finalized until construction is complete and water is delivered.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 27-28, Finding 7, Gender Analysis and Gender Action Plan
claims.paraphrase: Women expressed willingness to participate in water-user associations with training, but gender-role stereotypes, lower formal education and care burdens constrain sustained participation.
claims.limitations: The MTR describes constraints and planned support; sustained participation outcomes are not yet evaluated.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 49-50, ESIA/ESMP labor-recruitment risk assessment
claims.paraphrase: MTR flags possible underage hiring, gender discrimination, violence, worker conflict and grievance gaps from labor recruitment, especially in small Gasa.
claims.scenario: Prospective project-construction labor-influx safeguard risk; no climate scenario.
claims.limitations: Prospective safeguards risk only; no incidents or climate-attributed violence reported.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Labor recruitment may bring violence, worker conflict and grievance gaps in small Gasa; prospective risk only.

access_audit.notes: The official Bhutan CCDR PDF exceeded the browser tool's 10 MB content limit; the World Bank metadata/summary was not used for claims.
The 2024 National Centre for Hydrology and Meteorology climate projection PDF exceeded the browser tool's content-length limit; no search excerpt was used as a claim.
The National Environment Commission download URL timed out; the identical full report was accessed from the UNDP Bhutan publication page.

search_audit.query: Bhutan district and gewog climate vulnerability adaptive capacity risk map named locations
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the UNDP-hosted Bhutan district vulnerability assessment, national loss-and-damage findings and ACREWAS review. They identify district rankings, Lunana gewog, and specific flood-affected sites; coverage and data are incomplete.

search_audit.query: Bhutan climate change human mobility distress migration human wildlife conflict social cohesion report
search_audit.outcome: The government-UNDP assessment explicitly describes anecdotal climate-related distress migration, climate-linked human-wildlife conflict risk, and flood displacement affecting social cohesion. No inspected source documents climate-caused interpersonal or political violence.

search_audit.query: Bhutan conflict violence migration urbanization population growth effects on climate risk and adaptation delivery
search_audit.outcome: The district assessment associates in-migration, urbanisation and population growth with higher projected risk in Thimphu; ACREWAS lists prospective labor-influx safeguards risks in Gasa. No source documents political or communal violence as a barrier to adaptation delivery.

search_audit.query: Bhutan local water resilience capacity adaptation water user groups local government response review
search_audit.outcome: The NAP sets water-governance and local-capacity priorities; the ACREWAS review reports interim beneficiaries and training while noting limited delivered water access, participation barriers and emergency-response funding gaps.

gaps: No inspected source establishes climate-driven interpersonal, communal or political violence in Bhutan. The assessment's human-wildlife-conflict finding is not evidence of human social violence.
The climate-to-distress-mobility statement is described by the assessment as anecdotal; it gives no movement counts and does not link migration to later conflict.

The district vulnerability assessment uses older indicators, reports sparse annual Dzongkhag/Gewog data and uncertain cause-and-effect relationships; its rankings are not a current complete local survey.
The loss-and-damage assessment says loss records are fragmented and underreported; the Dechencholing and Punakha findings are case studies, not representative estimates.

The ACREWAS review is limited to three project Dzongkhags and a midterm period. Assured water access was not yet measurable as a household outcome, and the Gasa labor-influx passage identifies potential safeguards risks rather than reported incidents.
The World Bank CCDR and 2024 NCHM climate-projection PDF exceeded the browser tool's content limit; neither was used to support a claim.
